Stable 4.6.1 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/78bcf815-79d9-41db-9e03-2e5e31a0c0de PR https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e42b3d86-a79f-4086-a1d8-114474193fcd --- Stable moon https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/90ce5120-3966-4220-8a15-ea69b06f86c2 PR moon https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/66962018-e6e6-45a3-9b18-8e8f8ea31520 --- Both use these exposure settings: This PR makes auto exposure respond much more nicely in high contrast scenes, good example is the difference between ~0:31 in the first two videos. Stable keeps the image overexposed way too long and doesn't seem to react at all to the light passing through the atmosphere, while this PR makes appropriate adjustments. The moon videos are also a great example at how stable overexposes scenes for way too long. It is worth noting here that this pr does come with a visual impact, though given how big of an improvement this is, and that it makes the auto exposure actually usable and way more reliable I would say it is worth that cost. I'm not sure how many projects right now are using auto exposure due to it's unreliable nature and lack of artistic control. [Unreal Engine allows users to select an autoexposure metering mode](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/auto-exposure-in-unreal-engine#exposuremeteringmodes), maybe this is the way to go to ensure existing projects using auto exposure are not impacted? It does increase the scope of the PR. --- I did run into an issue (not sure how to reproduce, haven't been able to) where autoexposure started flickering a bit/acting unstable when I alt-tabbed and turns the scene fully black: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ca636e6c-9430-4229-bbef-f8be349d939f --- Going a bit out of my depth here, but I'm wondering if there's an opportunity here to provide more control over exposure behavior? For example, there's no control over the % of the screen that needs to be "bright" in order for the auto exposure to adjust. An issue I've been running into with this scene specifically is that despite increasing the max sensitivity, earth is always overexposed and at a certain point the max sensitivity doesn't change this exposure (The videos is as underexposed as I can get earth). I could make adjustments with the multiplier and scale sliders, but then the HDRI gets underexposed. There's probably some element of shader adjustments I should/could do, but at the same time it feels like I'm missing control over how the auto exposure is weighted, or tooling/information regarding the current brightness of the screen. I think if we were to go with the route of adding multiple metering modes, we do have an opportunity here to introduce a new auto exposure method that actually allows decent artistic control. Though obviously that becomes a much bigger scope.
